Connecting to stores

Source: vignettes/articles/connecting.Rmd
connecting.Rmd

Tutorials, catalogues and papers hand out Zarr addresses in many forms: s3:// and gs:// URIs, HTTPS URLs of the same objects, custom S3 endpoints, GDAL /vsi paths, and Python code full of storage_options. This article shows what to give zaro() for each, and what zaro does with it. The examples are shown, not run.

The short version

Give zaro() the address you have. Every object zaro fetches ends up as an HTTPS request through one curl connection pool whenever it can, so most forms work as they are.

You have Give zaro Notes
https://host/path/store.zarr the URL read with curl; needs consolidated metadata, or arrays =
s3://bucket/path, public the URI, with anonymous = TRUE known public buckets need nothing
s3://bucket/path, private the URI AWS keys in the environment, or arrow/GDAL credentials
S3-compatible service (CEPH, MinIO) s3:// with endpoint_override, or the HTTPS URL tenant:bucket names: use HTTPS
gs://bucket/path, public the URI, with anonymous = TRUE
a GDAL path, /vsicurl/..., /vsis3/... the path read through gdalraster, GDAL’s config applies
kerchunk, VirtualiZarr, byterefs reference+json://, virtualizarr://, byterefs://, flatrefs:// see virtual stores

HTTPS

Any static file server, object store or CDN that serves the store’s files over HTTPS works with the plain URL. zaro reads it with curl: no arrow, no GDAL.

eopf <- zaro("https://s3.explorer.eopf.copernicus.eu/esa-zarr-sentinel-explorer-fra/tests-output/sentinel-2-l2a/S2C_MSIL2A_20260120T084301_N0511_R064_T36UXA_20260120T122910.zarr")
zaro_groups(eopf)
r10m <- zaro_dataset(eopf, group = "measurements/reflectance/r10m")

HTTP can’t list a directory, so zaro needs the store’s consolidated metadata (.zmetadata for V2, a consolidated zarr.json for V3). Most published stores have it. If one doesn’t, name the arrays you want:

ds <- zaro_dataset("https://host/path/store.zarr", arrays = c("x", "y", "sst"))

An HTTPS URL of an S3 or GCS object (https://bucket.s3.region.amazonaws.com/..., https://storage.googleapis.com/bucket/...) is just another HTTPS URL and reads the same way. Use the s3:// or gs:// form when you need to list the store or sign the requests.

S3 

## public: say so, and give the region if you know it
store <- zaro("s3://aodn-cloud-optimised/model_sea_level_anomaly_gridded_realtime.zarr",
              anonymous = TRUE, region = "ap-southeast-2")

A few well-known public buckets (AODN, CMIP6 on GCS, NOAA and Pangeo buckets) are read anonymously without being asked. AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST=YES in the environment, or options(zaro.cloud_anonymous = TRUE), does the same for every bucket.

When the access is known like this, chunks go through the curl pool as HTTPS, many at once. The bucket’s region is read once from S3’s x-amz-bucket-region header if you don’t give it. Metadata and listings go through arrow when it is installed, otherwise through GDAL’s /vsis3/ (gdalraster).

For a private bucket, put the keys in the environment:

Sys.setenv(AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "...", AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = "...")
## AWS_SESSION_TOKEN too, for temporary credentials
store <- zaro("s3://my-bucket/path/store.zarr", region = "us-west-2")

zaro signs these requests itself (curl’s AWS SigV4), so they join the pool too. Other credentials (~/.aws profiles, instance roles) are left to arrow or GDAL, which read one object at a time: correct, but slower. zaro never guesses anonymous access for a bucket it doesn’t know, because S3 answers 403 for a missing object and a private bucket read anonymously would look like a store of empty chunks.

S3-compatible services

CEPH, MinIO, Wasabi and institutional object stores speak the S3 protocol at their own endpoint. Give the endpoint as endpoint_override (or set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL); objects are then addressed path-style, <endpoint>/<bucket>/<key>:

store <- zaro("s3://my-bucket/path/store.zarr",
              endpoint_override = "https://objects.example.org",
              anonymous = TRUE)

Without arrow, metadata is read through GDAL, which takes the endpoint from its own configuration: set AWS_S3_ENDPOINT (host only) and AWS_VIRTUAL_HOSTING=NO as well.

If the service is public, the HTTPS URL is simpler and avoids S3 client quirks entirely. CEPH, for example, names buckets tenant:bucket, which S3 clients reject as a bucket name. EODC’s object store is one such:

base <- "https://objects.eodc.eu/e05ab01a9d56408d82ac32d69a5aae2a:sample-data"
store <- zaro(paste0(base, "/tutorial_data/cpm_v253/S1A_IW_GRDH_1SDV_20220906T135439_20220906T135504_044885_055C76_B53F.zarr"))

To see what is in such a bucket, ask the endpoint for an S3 listing over plain HTTPS:

url <- paste0(base, "?prefix=tutorial_data/cpm_v253/&delimiter=/&max-keys=20")
cat(rawToChar(curl::curl_fetch_memory(url)$content))   # XML, one <Prefix> per store

GCS 

store <- zaro(paste0("gs://cmip6/CMIP6/ScenarioMIP/NOAA-GFDL/GFDL-ESM4/",
                     "ssp585/r1i1p1f1/Omon/zos/gn/v20180701"))   # known public
store <- zaro("gs://some-public-bucket/store.zarr", anonymous = TRUE)

Anonymous GCS chunks go through the pool as https://storage.googleapis.com/ URLs. Signed GCS access is left to arrow or GDAL.

GDAL paths

Any path starting /vsi opens a store read through gdalraster, so GDAL’s own configuration applies (AWS_*, GS_*, GDAL_HTTP_*, credentials files, /vsicurl/ options):

store <- zaro("/vsicurl/https://host/path/store.zarr")
store <- zaro("/vsis3/bucket/path/store.zarr")

Use this when you need something only GDAL handles, or to compare zaro’s own transport with GDAL’s.

Virtual stores

A reference store holds the URLs of other files: NetCDF, HDF5 or GeoTIFF archives, often in a bucket. zaro fetches those references through the same pool. They carry no anonymous or region of their own, so references to s3:// objects use the environment and options above (AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST, options(zaro.cloud_anonymous = TRUE), AWS keys, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL). byterefs stores can also remap their source paths, for example from a local mirror to a public HTTPS copy, with target; see virtual stores.

From Python

Python (fsspec, s3fs, xarray) zaro
storage_options={"anon": True}, anon=True anonymous = TRUE
client_kwargs={"endpoint_url": url} endpoint_override = url, or the HTTPS URL
{"token": "anon"} (gcsfs) anonymous = TRUE
{"key": ..., "secret": ...} AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
CEPH tenant:bucket handler workarounds the HTTPS URL
xr.open_zarr(url, group = g) zaro_dataset(url, group = g)
xr.open_datatree(url) zaro_groups(url), then zaro_dataset(group = )
fs.glob(...) zaro_list(), or an S3 listing over HTTPS

Options

Option Default
zaro.cloud_anonymous FALSE read every S3/GCS object anonymously
zaro.max_con 8 connections per host and in total
zaro.merge_gap 0 merge byte ranges this close on the same file
zaro.verbose TRUE report which backend opened the store

With zaro.verbose on, zaro() says which backend it chose and zaro_read() how many requests a read took, which is usually the quickest way to see whether a store is going through the pool.
